title: Irish Catholic Confederation
capsule: The Confederate Ireland (Confederation of Kilkenny) was an Irish Catholic self-governing council established in October 1642 following the Irish Rebellion of 1641, seeking to defend Catholic landowners and the rights of the Old English and Gaelic Irish against Protestant settlers and English parliamentary authority. At its greatest extent it controlled roughly two-thirds of Ireland, with its capital at Kilkenny; the Supreme Council engaged in complex diplomacy with the Stuart monarchy, the Papacy, and continental powers. Internal divisions between the Papal Nuncio Rinuccini and moderate Confederates weakened the confederation, and Oliver Cromwell's campaign of 1649–1650 systematically destroyed Confederate power, the remnant forces surrendering by 1653.

The Confederation's controlled territory is broadly documented in contemporary sources, but exact boundaries fluctuated with military campaigns and are not precisely cartographically fixed.
